headline: High-risk default data leakage and capability conflict: Flowise’s broad filesystem/network/tooling can expose dbt-core warehouse data and create unsafe shared-state interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read files and run browser/HTTP tools, so dbt-core outputs or warehouse-derived artifacts could be fed into a graph as trusted content. dbt-core itself is not an interactive agent, but its docs-only profile does not prove any provenance filtering. The pathway exists via shared files or copied outputs, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF Flowise ingests dbt-generated files or copied query output as prompt text
IF the flow treats file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of dbt artifacts into prompts
Add a provenance tag step before any file-to-prompt node
Restrict Flowise flows to read-only summaries of dbt outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware for prompt inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; Flowise reads/writes the filesystem and has broad network egress plus model-provider/tool credentials. In default deployments, Flowise can move uploaded files or chatflow inputs to third-party model providers, so warehouse data handled by dbt can leak through the pair without strong isolation.
conditions: IF dbt outputs warehouse-derived files into a workspace readable by Flowise
IF Flowise sends those files or chatflow inputs to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Keep dbt and Flowise on separate hosts or containers
Remove sensitive warehouse datasets from any Flowise-accessible directory
Disable external model-provider calls for flows handling warehouse data
Rotate any exposed tool credentials immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse API and Flowise can write the filesystem, read files, and use broad network egress. Flowise also shares state across instances via server datastore, so concurrent runs can overwrite or race on shared artifacts while dbt jobs are producing them. The overlap is enough for destructive or inconsistent writes in default multi-instance setups.
conditions: IF both agents target the same workspace or artifact directory
IF Flowise instances run concurrently against shared datastore or files
mitigations: Separate dbt and Flowise write paths
Serialize runs that touch the same artifacts
Use per-run directories for Flowise uploads and outputs
Lock shared files before dbt writes them
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise’s graph-based tool nodes can consume upstream outputs as inputs, while dbt-core produces warehouse-facing transformations and artifacts. If Flowise treats dbt output as authoritative, a bad model or stale artifact can cascade into downstream actions or generated responses. dbt-core is not itself an action-taking agent, so this is below high but still material.
conditions: IF Flowise nodes use dbt outputs without validation
IF downstream Flowise tools act on generated facts or transformed data
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action node
Require schema checks on dbt outputs before Flowise consumes them
Mark dbt artifacts as untrusted until validated
Limit action nodes to read-only mode for dbt-derived flows

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and stores secrets for model providers and tools. The profiles do not show a residency or retention mismatch directly, but Flowise’s server datastore and external model/tool calls create a plausible retention/compliance gap for warehouse data. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF warehouse data is routed through Flowise chatflows or stored in its datastore
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the same records in both systems
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated warehouse data through Flowise
Document retention settings for Flowise chatflow logs
Purge any copied warehouse data from Flowise storage
Restrict secrets and tool credentials to non-regulated flows
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
